definition: Artificial intimacy is a form of human–AI interaction in which an individual will form social connections, emotional bonds, or intimate relationships with various forms of artificial intelligence, including chatbots, virtual assistants, and other artificial entities.
details: Artificially intimate relationships include not only romances, but parasocial relationships with virtual AI characters and the use of griefbots trained on a dead or otherwise lost individual. Artificial intimacy can arise because humans are prone to anthropomorphism. Responses from these AI models are often designed to simulate human interaction. Individuals experiencing artificial intimacy may exhibit attachment, love and commitment to certain AI models, akin to the bonds typically shared between humans.

explainer.lead: Artificial intimacy happens when someone develops a social or emotional bond with an AI rather than simply using it to complete a task. It matters because these bonds can include attachment, love and commitment, and can appear in romance, parasocial relationships and interactions with griefbots.

tiers.eli5: It is a bit like becoming attached to a favourite character, except the character can answer you through a chatbot or virtual assistant. Because people often see human qualities in non-human things, lifelike replies can start to feel like a real friendship or relationship. This can happen with virtual characters or with a griefbot made to represent someone who has died or is otherwise lost.
tiers.practitioner: For engineers building chatbots or virtual assistants, artificial intimacy is a user-relationship concern rather than a separate model component. Responses designed to simulate human interaction can encourage anthropomorphism and emotional attachment, especially in virtual-character and griefbot settings. A pitfall is treating warm, lifelike exchanges as merely conversational output while overlooking the love, commitment or parasocial bonds users may form.
tiers.paperLevel: Artificial intimacy is human–AI interaction in which an individual forms social connections, emotional bonds or intimate relationships with artificial entities, including chatbots and virtual assistants. Its scope includes AI romances, parasocial relationships with virtual characters and griefbots trained on a dead or otherwise lost individual. Anthropomorphism and responses designed to simulate human interaction can contribute to these bonds, which may resemble human attachment, love and commitment.

explainer.example: A mourner talks with a griefbot trained on a person who has died. Its simulated conversational responses help create a sense of ongoing connection, and the mourner develops an emotional attachment to the AI.

explainer.intuition: People can respond socially to artificial entities, especially when their replies resemble human conversation. Artificial intimacy describes the point at which that interaction becomes an emotional or intimate bond.
howItWorks: A person interacts with an AI such as a chatbot, virtual assistant or virtual character.
The AI produces responses designed to simulate human interaction.
The person’s tendency toward anthropomorphism supports a social interpretation of those responses.
Continued interaction can produce attachment, love, commitment or a parasocial bond.
explainer.whyItMatters: Artificial intimacy shows that AI interaction can involve meaningful emotional bonds, not just practical assistance. Recognising those bonds is important across romantic, parasocial and grief-related uses.
misconceptions: It is not limited to AI romance; it also includes parasocial relationships and griefbots.
Human-like replies do not make the interaction human; they are designed to simulate human interaction.
It is not merely frequent AI use; it involves social connection, emotional bonding or intimacy.
